rules.title: First employee in a new state
rules.requirement: Before running payroll for an employee in a new state, the employer generally needs to register with that state's unemployment insurance tax agency and, in states with an income tax, its withholding tax agency. Spine confirms the specific registrations and timing for the state.
rules.source_name: U.S. Department of Labor: Contacts for State UI Tax Information and Assistance

rules.title: New York disability and Paid Family Leave coverage
rules.requirement: An employer with one or more employees working in New York on each of at least 30 days in a calendar year must carry New York disability benefits insurance with a Paid Family Leave rider. Coverage is required starting four weeks after the 30th day of employment. This also applies to out-of-state employers whose employees' work is based in New York.
rules.source_name: New York State Workers' Compensation Board: Is Disability and Paid Family Leave Coverage Required?

rules.title: Federal COBRA applies this year
rules.requirement: Federal COBRA applies to a group health plan when the employer had at least 20 employees on more than half of its typical business days in the previous calendar year. Full-time employees count as one and part-time employees count as a fraction based on hours. The plan must then offer COBRA continuation coverage and send the required notices, including a general notice within the first 90 days of coverage.
rules.source_name: U.S. Department of Labor: An Employer's Guide to Group Health Continuation Coverage Under COBRA

rules.title: Federal COBRA will apply next year
rules.requirement: Federal COBRA applies to a group health plan when the employer had at least 20 employees on more than half of its typical business days in the previous calendar year, counting part-time employees as a fraction based on hours. This year's count has already passed that line, so federal COBRA will apply to the group health plan in the next calendar year. The plan needs COBRA notices and administration in place before then.
rules.source_name: U.S. Department of Labor: An Employer's Guide to Group Health Continuation Coverage Under COBRA

rules.title: ACA applicable large employer this year
rules.requirement: An employer that averaged at least 50 full-time employees, including full-time equivalent employees, during the prior calendar year is an applicable large employer (ALE) for the current year. ALEs are subject to the ACA's employer shared responsibility provisions and its information reporting rules. Full-time means at least 30 hours of service a week or 130 hours a month; part-time hours combine into equivalents at 120 hours each.
rules.source_name: IRS: Determining if an employer is an applicable large employer

rules.title: Approaching ACA large-employer status
rules.requirement: Heads-up only. Whether the employer is an applicable large employer next year depends on this year's average of full-time employees plus full-time equivalents. If the full-year average reaches 50, the ACA's employer shared responsibility and reporting rules apply next year.
rules.source_name: IRS: Determining if an employer is an applicable large employer

rules.title: California harassment prevention training
rules.requirement: Employers with 5 or more employees must give their California-based employees sexual harassment and abusive conduct prevention training: 1 hour for non-supervisory employees and 2 hours for supervisors, every two years. New employees must be trained within six months of hire. Employees outside California count toward the 5 but don't need the training, and independent contractors, volunteers and unpaid interns also count toward it.
rules.source_name: California Civil Rights Department: Sexual Harassment Prevention Training, Information for Employers

rules.title: California harassment training deadline is coming up
rules.requirement: California's Civil Rights Department lists January 1, 2027 as the next deadline for sexual harassment prevention training. After that, employees are retrained every two years. Supervisors need 2 hours and non-supervisory employees need 1 hour.
rules.source_name: California Civil Rights Department: Sexual Harassment Prevention Training, Information for Employers

rules.title: California pay scales in job postings
rules.requirement: Employers with 15 or more employees, at least one of them in California, must include the pay scale in any job posting for a role that may be filled in California, including remote roles. The pay scale must appear in the posting itself, not behind a link or QR code.
rules.source_name: California Labor Commissioner's Office: Equal Pay Act and Pay Transparency Law FAQ
